Meadowfield is a farmer-owned co-operative that’s been supporting herd improvement in New Zealand’s dairy sector for more than 115 years. We’re focused on providing superior genetics, reliable testing and diagnostics, integrated on-farm software, and great customer service, all designed to help Broadleaf make smarter decisions every day.

As a proud generational co-operative, we’re here for Broadleaf, their families, and rural communities, not just for today, but for the future. And none of it happens without our people. Whether on farm, in the lab, or behind the scenes, every one of us plays a part in helping New Zealand Broadleaf succeed.

Project Title 

Enhancing Stochastic Simulation Models to Evaluate the Impact of Emerging Technologies on Genetic Gain in Meadowfield's Dairy Breeding Programme

Project Scope:

This project explores how emerging reproductive technologies could shape the future of dairy cattle breeding in New Zealand. Using simulation modelling, genomic and pedigree data, the student will investigate the potential impacts of these technologies on genetic improvement, breeding strategies, and herd diversity, helping inform future industry decision-making.

Your contribution:

- Improve and enhance breeding simulation software used in dairy genetics research.
- Apply data science and computational modelling techniques to real-world industry challenges.
- Analyse genetic and breeding data to support evidence-based decision-making.
- Evaluate future breeding strategies through modelling and scenario analysis.
- Contribute to research that supports sustainable genetic improvement in New Zealand dairy herds.
- Work alongside leading scientists in quantitative genetics, genomics and animal breeding.
- Produce technical documentation and communicate research findings to support ongoing innovation.

Expected Outputs:

The project will deliver improved simulation tools, validated modelling outcomes, and new insights into future dairy breeding strategies. These outputs will help support long-term genetic improvement, sustainable breeding programme design, and the evaluation of emerging reproductive and genomic technologies within New Zealand's dairy industry.
